about.title: A little about me.
paragraphs: I have always been curious about how things work, and computers were the first thing that hooked me. I started on my own and later made it formal with a Higher Vocational Degree in Cross-platform Application Development at U-tad and a Python bootcamp.

Since then I have worked in banking, in a tax product and in management software with more than 25 years of history. I like to understand the whole problem before touching code, and I am just as comfortable polishing an interface as setting up deployment.

With AI I do two different things: I use it to work better, and I build solutions that integrate it, like the agents and automations in my products. The first speeds me up; the second solves problems. Neither replaces knowing engineering.

experience.title: Where I have been.
experience.hint: Open each stop to see what I did there.

items.role: Lead Frontend and Full Stack Developer
points: Full modernization of the interface of a DMS with more than 25 years on the market, using JavaScript and Figma design.
Architecture analysis to renew the corporate portal and leadership of the migration to WordPress to integrate the blog and SEO.
Led the development from scratch of a RESTful API portal, with endpoints documented in YAML.
Refactored legacy ColdFusion code to an MVC architecture and optimized SQL queries to cut response times.
Worked with Jira, version control and technical documentation in Confluence.
Design and build of my own products, from idea to deployment.
Stibios Agent Platform: autonomous agents built with LangGraph and Gemini that generate content and leads for several projects and report through Telegram.
Designed and built from scratch the website of an independent fashion magazine, aligned with its editorial identity.
SEO-optimized structure and a custom content manager so the editorial team can update the site on their own.
Ongoing maintenance, visual tweaks and technical support.
Improvements to the frontend (JavaScript) and backend (PHP) of a monitoring system, optimizing interfaces and data loading.
Automated and functional tests to validate each change before deployment.
Collaboration in DevOps environments with development, test and production virtual machines.
Worked closely with the product team to turn user needs into features.
Built Me Asesoran Rentas, backend and frontend: integration with the Spanish government API and authentication system, and validation and submission of tax returns by tax advisors.

work.title: What already works.

items.name: MadRing Guide
items.text: A PWA to follow the Spanish F1 Grand Prix at the MADRING circuit in Madrid, with the week's schedule, transport, circuit zones and live timing. It draws the cars' positions in real time on a track generated from the telemetry itself, with no per-circuit illustration.
items.imageAlt: MadRing Guide home screen: countdown and shortcuts to schedule, zones, transport and F1 data.
items.role: Product, design, frontend, backend, database, deployment and SEO.
items.period: August – September 2026. Launched at the GP on 11–13 September.
points: A proxy with a 25 s cache, single-flight and staggered requests keeps within the OpenF1 rate limits however much traffic there is.
The schedule is rendered on the server so search engines and AI assistants can read it without running JavaScript.

items.name: Stibios Agent Platform
items.text: A platform of autonomous AI agents, running 24/7, that generate content, analyze trends and qualify leads for several projects: Revista Victoria, MadRing and Blog Stibios. It orchestrates LangGraph graphs with Gemini 2.5, publishes to Sanity and Supabase and reports through Telegram with no human intervention.
items.imageAlt: Stibios Agents dashboard: a status card for each agent and a table of the latest runs.
items.role: Full stack developer and architect: complete design of the platform, all the agents and the infrastructure.
points: Eight agents are in production: news, dev briefing, blogs (Stibios, Victoria and Pádel), leads, trends and the MadRing scraper.
They run on GitHub Actions, with cron and manual runs, with no server of my own.
